> Pi writes the code and you decide what it means. Ask it to use `ps_species`
> and `ps_genes` from the setup chunk. The pipeline it will use has three knobs:
> `tax_transform() |> dist_calc() |> ord_calc("PCoA") |> ord_plot()`

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(microViz)
library(phyloseq)

source(here("R/count_tables.R"))

# The grouping you built and saved in notebook 02. If it is not there yet, this
# stops with a clear message instead of a confusing one.
groups_file <- here("data/my_sample_groups.csv")
if (!file.exists(groups_file)) {
  stop("Could not find ", groups_file,
       "\nGo back to notebook 02, Exercise 2, step 5 and save your per-sample ",
       "table with the `community` column. Or rebuild it here: the Lactobacillus ",
       "fraction from the species table, split at 0.5.", call. = FALSE)
}
sample_groups <- read_csv(groups_file)

# as_counts() builds a phyloseq object from either count table. For the gene
# table it hands microViz the gene annotation as the rank table, which is why
# every microViz verb below works on genes.
ps_species <- as_counts(table = "microbiome")
ps_genes   <- as_counts(table = "rnaseq", min_count = 10, min_samples = 100)
```

```{r}
ps_species
ps_genes
```

```{r}
# Add your community column to both objects so you can colour by it.
add_groups <- function(ps) {
  sd <- as(sample_data(ps), "data.frame") |>
    rownames_to_column("sid") |>
    left_join(sample_groups |> select(sample_id, community, lacto_fraction),
              by = c("sid" = "sample_id")) |>
    column_to_rownames("sid")
  sample_data(ps) <- sample_data(sd)
  ps
}

ps_species <- add_groups(ps_species)
ps_genes   <- add_groups(ps_genes)
```

# Exercise 1: The species table

## Part 1 — Predict (no code)

**1. Our species table is about 89% zeros. Will Bray-Curtis or Jaccard separate the community types more clearly?**

- *Your answer:*

```{r}
library(microViz)

bray_plot <- ps_species |>
  tax_transform("identity", rank = "species") |>
  dist_calc("bray") |>
  ord_calc("PCoA") |>
  ord_plot(colour = "community")

jaccard_plot <- ps_species |>
  tax_transform("binary", rank = "species") |>
  dist_calc("jaccard") |>
  ord_calc("PCoA") |>
  ord_plot(colour = "community")

bray_plot
jaccard_plot

ggsave("plots/bray.png", bray_plot, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
ggsave("plots/jaccard.png", jaccard_plot, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
run_test <- function(distance_name, transform_name) {
  result <- ps_species |>
    tax_transform(transform_name, rank = "species") |>
    dist_calc(distance_name) |>
    dist_permanova(variables = "community", n_perms = 999, seed = 1) |>
    perm_get() |>
    as.data.frame()

  tibble::tibble(
    distance = distance_name,
    R2 = result["community", "R2"],
    F = result["community", "F"],
    p_value = result["community", "Pr(>F)"]
  )
}

dplyr::bind_rows(
  run_test("bray", "identity"),
  run_test("jaccard", "binary")
)


results <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  run_test("bray", "identity"),
  run_test("jaccard", "binary")
)

results

formatted_results <- results |>
  gtsummary::tbl_summary(
    by = distance,
    include = c(R2, F, p_value),
    type = list(
      R2 ~ "continuous",
      F ~ "continuous",
      p_value ~ "continuous"
    ),
    statistic = list(gtsummary::all_continuous() ~ "{mean}"),
    digits = list(R2 ~ 3, F ~ 1, p_value ~ 3),
    missing = "no"
  ) |>
  gtsummary::modify_header(
    label = "**Measure**",
    gtsummary::all_stat_cols() ~ "**{level}**"
  ) |>
  gtsummary::bold_labels()

gt::gtsave(
  gtsummary::as_gt(formatted_results),
  filename = here::here("plots/formatted_results.html")
)

formatted_results
```


**2. Shuffling `outcome` randomly across 471 samples, what R2 would PERMANOVA report?**

- *Your answer:*

```{r}

get_outcome_r2 <- function(ps) {
  ps |>
    tax_transform("identity", rank = "species") |>
    dist_calc("bray") |>
    dist_permanova(variables = "outcome", n_perms = 999, seed = 1) |>
    perm_get() |>
    as.data.frame() |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("term") |>
    dplyr::filter(term == "outcome") |>
    dplyr::pull(R2)
}

# R² using the original outcome labels
observed_r2 <- get_outcome_r2(ps_species)

# Shuffle outcome labels across samples, keeping the species data unchanged
set.seed(2026)
ps_shuffled <- ps_species
metadata <- as.data.frame(phyloseq::sample_data(ps_shuffled))
metadata$outcome <- sample(metadata$outcome)
phyloseq::sample_data(ps_shuffled) <- phyloseq::sample_data(metadata)

shuffled_r2 <- get_outcome_r2(ps_shuffled)

tibble::tibble(
  labels = c("Original outcome", "Shuffled outcome"),
  R2 = c(observed_r2, shuffled_r2)
) # it will sit at p028 week 18
```



**3. Where will the 438-read sample sit in a Bray-Curtis ordination?**

- *Your answer:*

```{r}

counts <- as(phyloseq::otu_table(ps_species), "matrix")
if (phyloseq::taxa_are_rows(ps_species)) {
  counts <- t(counts)
}

low_read_id <- rownames(counts)[rowSums(counts) == 438]
stopifnot(length(low_read_id) == 1)

bray <- vegan::vegdist(counts, method = "bray")
ordination <- cmdscale(bray, k = 2)

plot_data <- data.frame(
  sample_id = rownames(ordination),
  Axis1 = ordination[, 1],
  Axis2 = ordination[, 2],
  community = phyloseq::sample_data(ps_species)$community
)

cat("438-read sample:", low_read_id, "\n")

plot_data

# Its position on the two ordination axes
plot_data |>
  dplyr::filter(sample_id == low_read_id) |>
  print()

# The five most similar samples by Bray-Curtis distance
bc <- as.matrix(bray)
nearest <- sort(bc[low_read_id, setdiff(rownames(bc), low_read_id)])
head(nearest, 5)

p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(Axis1, Axis2, colour = community)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_label(
    data = subset(plot_data, sample_id == low_read_id),
    aes(label = sample_id),
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(title = "Bray-Curtis PCoA: 438-read sample")

ggplot2::ggsave(
  "plots/bray_438_sample.png",
  plot = p,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```

```{r}

bray <- vegan::vegdist(counts, method = "bray")

# Calculate the first two PCoA axes and their share of positive variation
ordination <- cmdscale(bray, k = 2, eig = TRUE)
points <- ordination$points
positive_eigenvalues <- ordination$eig[ordination$eig > 0]
axis_percent <- 100 * ordination$eig[1:2] / sum(positive_eigenvalues)

# Compare the 438-read sample's mean distance with the overall mean pairwise distance
bc <- as.matrix(bray)
other_ids <- setdiff(rownames(bc), low_read_id)
sample_mean <- mean(bc[low_read_id, other_ids])
overall_pairwise_mean <- mean(bc[lower.tri(bc)])

cat(sprintf(
  "%s mean distance to all other samples: %.3f\nOverall mean pairwise distance: %.3f\n",
  low_read_id, sample_mean, overall_pairwise_mean
))

plot_data <- data.frame(
  sample_id = rownames(points),
  Axis1 = points[, 1],
  Axis2 = points[, 2],
  community = as.data.frame(phyloseq::sample_data(ps_species))[
    rownames(points), "community"
  ]
)

p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(Axis1, Axis2, colour = community)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_label(
    data = subset(plot_data, sample_id == low_read_id),
    aes(label = sample_id),
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Bray-Curtis PCoA: 438-read sample",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "438-read sample mean distance: %.3f; overall pairwise mean: %.3f",
      sample_mean, overall_pairwise_mean
    ),
    x = sprintf("Axis 1 (%.1f%%)", axis_percent[1]),
    y = sprintf("Axis 2 (%.1f%%)", axis_percent[2])
  )

ggplot2::ggsave(
  "plots/bray_438_sample.png",
  plot = p,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)

```


```{r}
counts <- as(phyloseq::otu_table(ps_species), "matrix")
if (phyloseq::taxa_are_rows(ps_species)) {
  counts <- t(counts)  # Make samples rows and species columns
}

low_read_id <- rownames(counts)[rowSums(counts) == 438]
if (length(low_read_id) != 1) {
  stop("Expected one sample with 438 reads; found ", length(low_read_id), ".")
}

# Bray-Curtis distances between samples
bray <- vegan::vegdist(counts, method = "bray")
bc <- as.matrix(bray)

# Compare the 438-read sample's mean distance with the overall pairwise mean
other_samples <- setdiff(rownames(bc), low_read_id)
mean_distance_from_438 <- mean(bc[low_read_id, other_samples])
overall_mean_pairwise_distance <- mean(bc[lower.tri(bc)])

cat(sprintf(
  "%s mean distance to other samples: %.3f\nOverall mean pairwise distance: %.3f\n",
  low_read_id, mean_distance_from_438, overall_mean_pairwise_distance
))

# PCoA coordinates and the share of positive variation on each axis
ordination <- cmdscale(bray, k = 2, eig = TRUE)
points <- ordination$points
positive_eigenvalues <- ordination$eig[ordination$eig > 0]
axis_percent <- 100 * ordination$eig[1:2] / sum(positive_eigenvalues)

metadata <- as.data.frame(phyloseq::sample_data(ps_species))
plot_data <- data.frame(
  sample_id = rownames(points),
  Axis1 = points[, 1],
  Axis2 = points[, 2],
  community = metadata[rownames(points), "community"]
)

p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(Axis1, Axis2, colour = community)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_point() +
  ggplot2::geom_label(
    data = subset(plot_data, sample_id == low_read_id),
    ggplot2::aes(label = sample_id),
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Bray-Curtis PCoA: 438-read sample",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "mean_distance_from_438: %.3f; overall_mean_pairwise_distance: %.3f",
      mean_distance_from_438, overall_mean_pairwise_distance
    ),
    x = sprintf("Axis 1 (%.1f%%)", axis_percent[1]),
    y = sprintf("Axis 2 (%.1f%%)", axis_percent[2])
  )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
ggplot2::ggsave(
  "plots/bray_438_sample.png",
  plot = p,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```


```{r}
counts <- as(phyloseq::otu_table(ps_species), "matrix")
if (phyloseq::taxa_are_rows(ps_species)) {
  counts <- t(counts)  # Samples are rows; species are columns
}

low_read_id <- rownames(counts)[rowSums(counts) == 438]
if (length(low_read_id) != 1) {
  stop("Expected one sample with 438 reads; found ", length(low_read_id), ".")
}

# Convert each sample to relative abundances
library_sizes <- rowSums(counts)
if (any(library_sizes == 0)) {
  stop("Cannot calculate relative abundances: at least one sample has zero reads.")
}
relative_counts <- sweep(counts, 1, library_sizes, "/")

# Bray-Curtis distances on relative abundances
bray <- vegan::vegdist(relative_counts, method = "bray")
bc <- as.matrix(bray)

# Mean distance from the 438-read sample and overall mean across unique pairs
other_samples <- setdiff(rownames(bc), low_read_id)
mean_distance_from_438 <- mean(bc[low_read_id, other_samples])
overall_mean_pairwise_distance <- mean(bc[lower.tri(bc)])

print(data.frame(
  sample_id = low_read_id,
  reads = library_sizes[low_read_id],
  mean_distance_from_438 = mean_distance_from_438,
  overall_mean_pairwise_distance = overall_mean_pairwise_distance
))

# Calculate PCoA coordinates and the share of positive variation per axis
ordination <- cmdscale(bray, k = 2, eig = TRUE)
points <- ordination$points
positive_eigenvalues <- ordination$eig[ordination$eig > 0]
axis_percent <- 100 * ordination$eig[1:2] / sum(positive_eigenvalues)

metadata <- as.data.frame(phyloseq::sample_data(ps_species))
plot_data <- data.frame(
  sample_id = rownames(points),
  Axis1 = points[, 1],
  Axis2 = points[, 2],
  community = metadata[rownames(points), "community"]
)

p <- ggplot2::ggplot(
  plot_data,
  ggplot2::aes(Axis1, Axis2, colour = community)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_point() +
  ggplot2::geom_label(
    data = subset(plot_data, sample_id == low_read_id),
    ggplot2::aes(label = sample_id),
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Bray-Curtis PCoA: 438-read sample",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "mean_distance_from_438: %.3f; overall_mean_pairwise_distance: %.3f",
      mean_distance_from_438, overall_mean_pairwise_distance
    ),
    x = sprintf("Axis 1 (%.1f%%)", axis_percent[1]),
    y = sprintf("Axis 2 (%.1f%%)", axis_percent[2])
  )

dir.create("plots", showWarnings = FALSE)
ggplot2::ggsave(
  "plots/bray_438_sample.png",
  plot = p,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```

# Code from pi
```{r}

source(here::here("R/count_tables.R"))
library(vegan)

d <- read_counts("instructional")
lib <- colSums(d$species)

if (any(lib == 0)) {
  stop("A sample has zero reads, so its relative abundances cannot be calculated.")
}

# Calculate relative abundances, then Bray-Curtis distances between samples
rel <- sweep(d$species, 2, lib, "/")
bc_dist <- vegdist(t(rel), method = "bray")
pco <- cmdscale(bc_dist, k = 2)

# Colour samples by library-size group and save the plot
depth_group <- cut(lib, breaks = 3)
png("plots/library_depth_pcoa.png", width = 900, height = 700)
plot(pco, col = as.integer(depth_group), pch = 19,
     xlab = "PCoA axis 1", ylab = "PCoA axis 2")
legend("topright", legend = levels(depth_group),
       col = seq_along(levels(depth_group)), pch = 19,
       title = "Library size")
dev.off()

# Find the sample with exactly 438 reads
sample_438 <- names(lib)[lib == 438]
if (length(sample_438) != 1) {
  stop("Expected one sample with 438 reads; found ", length(sample_438), ".")
}

# Compare its mean distance to other samples with the overall mean pairwise distance
bc <- as.matrix(bc_dist)
other_samples <- setdiff(colnames(bc), sample_438)

data.frame(
  sample_id = sample_438,
  reads = unname(lib[sample_438]),
  mean_distance_from_438 = mean(bc[sample_438, other_samples]),
  overall_mean_pairwise_distance = mean(bc[lower.tri(bc)])
)
```

### Step 1: the first ordination

Suggested request: *Using `ps_species` from the setup chunk, make a Bray-Curtis
PCoA with microViz at the species level and colour it by `community`. Put the
share of variation on each axis title.*

```{r}
bray_plot <- ps_species |>
  microViz::tax_transform("identity", rank = "species") |>
  microViz::dist_calc("bray") |>
  microViz::ord_calc("PCoA") |>
  microViz::ord_plot(colour = "community")

# Save the plot so you can open it in VS Code
```
